item.text: {"text":"[TiSASRec (2020)](https://jiachengli1995.github.io/files/wsdm20.pdf) supplies the foundational mechanism: learned pairwise time-interval embeddings alongside positional information, with ablations examining their contributions. Its temporal mechanism is transferable to BERT4Rec without adopting its causal backbone. [TemProxRec (2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.09784) extends temporal modeling through absolute/relative temporal and positional embeddings plus contrastive learning across users interacting during similar periods. [LSTASRec (2025 preprint)](https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/Delivery.cfm/fc04baa1-18bd-42b2-aa9b-ea2414f684df-MECA.pdf?abstractid=5238143&mirid=1) describes normalized relative-time attention biases and separate long-/short-term interest extraction. These support temporal relevance beyond sequence position; they do not establish gains under this pinned Amazon benchmark.\n\nPractical hypothesis, inferred from these mechanisms: retain one jointly trained bidirectional BERT4Rec and add per-head bucketed log-time-gap biases, optionally a learned nonnegative decay penalty. Heads with near-zero decay could retain persistent interests; stronger decay could emphasize bursts. Use observed history-to-history gaps; for appended MASK, anchor temporal features to the latest observed event and explicitly encode the query’s unknown timestamp. Never supply the held-out event time, including during terminal-mask training. Preserve masked-target training and final nonpadding MASK readout. Compare positional-only attention, fixed decay, learned positional recency, relative-time bias, and bias plus adaptive decay under identical budgets. The key unresolved question is whether elapsed time adds validation HR@10 beyond positional recency, rather than merely increasing model capacity."}
